artifactType: Editorial integration handoff; not a registered Study or daily queue entry
title: Stop the three-peat

contract.question: Will the Eagles win Super Bowl 2025?
contract.rules: YES if Philadelphia wins Super Bowl LIX; otherwise NO. Elimination under NFL rules allowed immediate NO. This is the season-long Eagles championship contract, not the later Eagles–Chiefs match-winner contract.

selection.disclosure: Selection was frozen before the fresh event-window calculation. Prior project records exposed measurements for some reused Eagles events; this is a prospective selection freeze, not a claim of blinded preregistration. No card was substituted after seeing these results.

dataset.rejectionRule: Five Polymarket prices above 1.0 were rejected; no clipping.
dataset.markPolicy: Latest source price per hourly bucket, treated as a trade under the project importer convention; API freshness, spread, and volume are not established.

cards.title: Eagles lose 22–21 after Atlanta’s late touchdown
cards.timingDecision: Gamebook-derived final whistle is earlier than the recap modification. Preserve the later recap public cutoff because the gamebook does not prove the first public report; no scoring correction.
cards.claim: Atlanta drove 70 yards for a final-minute touchdown and defeated Philadelphia 22–21.
cards.mechanism: A home loss driven by late-game execution can lower confidence in coaching, defense, and close-game reliability.
cards.competingExplanation: The lead evaporated during a televised game; other Week 2 results and the full NFC comparison set also updated inside the window. This is not a clean pre-kickoff-to-final comparison.

cards.title: Saquon Barkley rushes for an Eagles-record 255 yards
cards.timingDecision: Gamebook-derived final whistle is earlier than the team feature publication/modification. Preserve the later public cutoff because the gamebook does not prove when the record first became public; no scoring correction.
cards.claim: Philadelphia beat the Rams 37–20 for its seventh straight win while Barkley rushed for 255 yards.
cards.mechanism: A dominant road performance with an elite rushing identity can strengthen both seeding expectations and playoff matchup resilience.
cards.competingExplanation: The record accumulated during the whole game; the result, other Week 12 and Thanksgiving results, health news, and changing NFC standings share the window.

cards.title: Hurts leaves with a concussion as Washington ends the Eagles’ winning streak
cards.timingDecision: Gamebook verifies the final result and the Hurts injury play sequence. Preserve the later live-recap cutoff because first public injury confirmation and public completion are not established by the gamebook; no scoring correction.
cards.claim: Jalen Hurts left with a concussion and Washington defeated Philadelphia 36–33, ending a ten-game Eagles winning streak.
cards.mechanism: Quarterback health immediately affects playoff readiness, while the loss weakens the path to the NFC’s top seed.
cards.competingExplanation: Keep the concussion, replacement-quarterback performance, and loss as one information cluster. Week 16 results inside the window changed the NFC seeding race and playoff field; later injury updates also matter.

cards.title: Eagles survive the Rams in the snow, 28–22
cards.timingDecision: Gamebook verifies the snow-game final whistle before the live-recap modification. Preserve the later public cutoff because no immutable first-public record is captured; no scoring correction.
cards.claim: Philadelphia defeated the Rams 28–22 in snowy conditions and advanced to the NFC Championship.
cards.mechanism: Survival sharply reduces the remaining tournament tree and preserves home-field advantage for the conference final.
cards.competingExplanation: The other divisional results (including the Chiefs–Texans, Lions–Commanders, and Bills–Ravens games) changed the remaining playoff field and opponent tree in the same broad window. Weather and late turnovers add performance noise.

cards.title: Eagles score 55 to reach the Super Bowl
cards.timingDecision: Gamebook verifies the NFC title final whistle before the team analysis modification. Preserve the later public cutoff because the gamebook does not establish first public completion and the AFC result was also available; no scoring correction.
cards.claim: Philadelphia defeated Washington 55–23 and advanced to Super Bowl LIX.
cards.mechanism: Winning the conference removes every remaining path except the single Super Bowl matchup.
cards.competingExplanation: The AFC Championship result and the resulting opponent/matchup field arrived in the same evening and delayed window. Treat the observed movement as a mixed playoff-weekend response; do not score the Super Bowl itself.

ranking.comparisonPolicy: Observed stabilized minus reference medians; tie threshold is one percentage point and is not transitive; no nonzero attribution share; no headline-alone causality.

ending.text: Philadelphia beat Kansas City 40–22 in Super Bowl LIX on February 9, 2025, denying the Chiefs a third consecutive Super Bowl victory. The provider resolved the Eagles championship contract YES. Keep the Super Bowl itself entirely in the ending.
